1.note: Pligo is the Italian plico, a packet or bundle (of letters). This line is the last line of the page lost in the archive.org copy, read from the copy of the 1885 printing at the National Library of Israel (S 32 A 1051).

2.note: שמ"ל = שמן למאור, "oil for the lamp" (lit in a synagogue for the rest of a soul). Sefer ha-Zikkaron (part 11) spells out the same act: בימ"ת נתתי צדקה ושמן למאו' למנוחת אבא מארי ומ' אמי.

3.note: ההי"ב = ה' הטוב יכפר בעד, "may the good Lord pardon" (2 Chr 30:18); the Ḥida writes the prayer out in full in part 8 (paragraph 111).

4.note: So printed (checked on the scan). Probably a misprint or an abbreviation; the usual pair is "keen and learned" (חריף ובקי). Left as uncertain.

5.note: So printed. Read as "with the help of the Almighty" (Shaddai); the extra mem is not explained.

6.note: Unclear place name: perhaps the beach or the outer anchorage of Livorno (Italian spiaggia?). The OCR reading לשלים was not checked against the scan.

7.note: Pan esponjado (Spanish), sponge bread; so A. Freimann, Ma'agal Tov ha-Shalem (Berlin–Jerusalem 1921–34), p. 66, n. 8. Signor Pereira's gift just before is pan di Spagna, the Italian sponge cake.

8.note: A play on Josh 2:5, ויהי השער לסגור, "when the gate was about to be shut": the Ḥida writes הצער, "the grief", for השער, "the gate", and adds "my heart"; the abbreviation mark points to the change of one letter.

9.note: חלי"ש = חיים לישראל שבק, "he left life to Israel", a formula for a righteous man's death; so A. Freimann, Ma'agal Tov ha-Shalem (Berlin–Jerusalem 1921–34), p. 66, n. 9.
